utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who told you on the 26th of January, 1993 to collect the captured persons in Lasva?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. We did not collect anybody there. We just took them over.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So who was in Zenica - the person - who told you to take the prisoners over from Lasva?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion of the military police, through my superior, Bakir Alispahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And during your travel to Lasva and on the spot, who was in charge of the 3rd Corps Military Police Staff during the takeover or transfer of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Lasva itself, to which ABiH soldiers present there did you speak first?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them. I believe that they were members of the 2nd PDO and members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you remember any names of the commander or of the persons you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So did you speak outside of the school to these persons? Did you enter a building?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was at the entrance to the building. I remember that there was no light. It was already dark. And the members of the military unit that had participated in combat on that day, I spoke to them at the entrance to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did they tell you, these members of the military units?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: They told me more or less something along the following lines: That there is no problem, that they would hand over the prisoners of war to us after certain consultations with their superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know who their own superiors were, or were you present when they consulted their own superiors?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't present and I don't know who their superiors were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You yourself, did you ever enter the elementary school in Lasva?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You testified that there was - and I quote - "an unpleasant situation on the ground" in Lasva. What do you mean by "unpleasant situation on the ground"?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I meant what I said. For me it was an unpleasant situation because there were a lot of civilians and a lot of soldiers there. It was noisy, and I had a mission to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was your impression? Who was, before you arrived, in charge of the prisoners? Was it the members from the 2nd, I think, Battalion of the Zenica Municipal Defence Staff, or was it, rather, the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure who it was. I know that these two units were active in the area. I really don't know who was in charge of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many men altogether did you take back to Zenica? I mean prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that there were approximately 20 of them. I can't be sure of their exact number. Twenty or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that there was one prisoner who had difficulties of some kind who was put in a car. He couldn't walk. Was he injured? Can you please just tell.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: A member of the military police informed me that one of the prisoners was complaining of pain, that he had problems walking. He could walk, but he had problems walking. I did not see any visible injuries on his body, but I myself could see that he had problems walking. I ordered for this prisoner to be put in the passenger vehicle and to sit in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were you aware that all prisoners were going to the Zenica KP Dom, or was there a few other prisoners who were going in another direction? Did you see everybody boarding the bus before you left with the car?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: All the prisoners of war that I took over boarded the bus, and they were all brought to the Zenica KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there a second person who took over other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: While I was there, nobody else was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you left, were there any prisoners of war remaining in Lasva? I mean, you hadn't looked in the school itself, but did you see that a few Croat prisoners stayed in Lasva?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. The prisoners that I took over were transferred to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in Lasva itself, did you see Dragan Rados boarding the bus to the KP Dom Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I didn't know who Dragan Rados was. On the following day, I spoke to him and I know that he is the man who boarded the bus on that day. He was taken to the KP Dom. And on the following day, he was one of the persons whom I interviewed, Dragan Rados.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you positively saw him entering the bus, which was then driven to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: At the moment when I was taking the prisoners over, I didn't know who Dragan Rados was. On the following day, I spoke to three prisoners and Dragan Rados was among them. So I know for a fact that he was amongst those who had boarded the buses, who had been taken to the JNA centre, and he was among the three with whom I spoke on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned in your testimony that somebody talked in Lasva about battle casualties. Who exactly was this person? Do you remember anything, from which ABiH unit this person was, his name?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No. I've told you that the soldiers were mixed with the civilians, and I really can't remember who it was in the crowd, who said that. It was dark and there were a lot of people there. But I learnt that in the combat that had taken place that day, earlier that day, that there were casualties on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What exactly did you learn about the casualties? A number, an event?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Nothing precise. I only learnt that on the BiH army side Camdzic was killed together with another member, and also that the commander of the area of the HVO, Zvonko Rajic, was also killed. And this is all the information that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned three names: Viktor Rajic, Dragan Rados, and a person you described as Kristo. If I may ask: Would it refresh your recollection if this person is called Anto Kristo or Franjo Kristo? I'm just asking. Maybe you recall.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Kristo is a very popular name, and the first name is either Franjo or Anto or Stipe, which is again a popular name. But I remember him because he told me that he worked at the national theatre of Zenica, and that's how I remember him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who tasked you the next day, on the 27th of January, to take the statements?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: The investigative judge of the district court was already involved in the investigation. We received our orders from him, the order -- the orders to collect information. We received this order from the battalion command, to -- to collect the statements. And -- and the MUP was involved in the rest of the crime investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: There were only four or five such judges at the time, and I believe that on that particular occasion it was Mirsad Strika who was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many statements were taken altogether, not only by you but maybe by your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Maybe four or five. And I took three statements. And if you multiply that by the number of us, you will arrive at a number of maybe 15 to 20. And that pretty much equals the number of prisoners that we had brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So I take it virtually every of these prisoners who were taken or transferred from Lasva to KP Dom were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I cannot be sure of that. I can't be positive of that. I know that I took three statements. I don't know who else took any other statements, whether all the prisoners were interviewed or not. I suppose that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these statements, did you write the statements down and have the interrogated person sign it at the end?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is how we worked, and we forwarded the statements to be enclosed with the court file, because we worked at the request of the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you want to say that you forwarded them to Judge Strika, the investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, to Judge Strika, who was in charge of the investigation. And we also forwarded an official record to the military security services centre via our battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you write also your own assessment after having taken these statements, what transpired out of these statements? Do you recall that you wrote something maybe to your superior?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes. More or less what I've already said in response to Mrs. Residovic's questions. These members of the HVO, these prisoners, mostly wanted to mitigate their responsibility and their participation. They expressed regret, but none of them told me anything that might have pointed to something illegal having taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you or your colleagues perform an on-site visit in Dusina proper?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, because the duty judge in the district military court took over the case, and as I have already said, in such cases he is in charge of the investigation and he issues orders. It is only upon his instructions that it is possible to take any measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So I understand that no on-site visit was being -- taking place.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, I personally didn't make such a visit, and if the duty judge had given such instructions, it would have been done. Now, why it wasn't, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would the 3rd Corps military police normally be the unit who would perform such an on-site visit, since you had interviewed already a few prisoners of war? Would the 3rd Corps military police have done such an on-site visit?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: It would be customary if we had received such orders from the duty judge in the district military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When foreigners were suspected of being involved in crimes and then the Rules of Service of the military police of the ABiH envisaged mandatory cooperation between the MUP and the CSB -- between the 3rd Corps military police, on the one hand side, and the MUP and the CSB, on the other hand side. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I said that if civilians had taken part in committing crimes which are prosecuted by -- ex officio and if military property had been stolen or damaged and, in the case of criminal offences that I have already listed, then cooperation is established with the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, can I just distribute P328. These are the Rules of the Service of the military police of the ABiH, and I'm referring to section 50, the last sentence of section 50. This is contained in Chapter 2, "Military police services," under the heading 7, "Crime prevention service."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is page 22. I'm only interested in the last sentence. Can you please read the last sentence out loud.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Did you say paragraph 50?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 50, yes. Last sentence.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: "When we are talking about military offences that the military police has to investigate, when the perpetrator or accomplice of a criminal offence is a citizen of the republic who is not a member of the armed forces or a foreign citizen without diplomatic status, the necessary measure shall be taken by the authorised official of the military police in collaboration with the competent MUP organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the reason for ordering a mandatory cooperation between, for example, the 3rd Corps military police and the Zenica CSB in case that a foreigner is suspected of being a perpetrator of a crime? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I think I've already explained how we cooperated with the Security Services Centre and MUP. If we are talking about criminal offences that are prosecuted, such as the foundations of the social order and crimes against the armed forces committed by civilians or by a foreigner, in that case cooperation had to be established with the CSB and the MUP. So the military police in that case was not independent in performing its duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So whenever a foreigner was involved, basically cooperation with the CSB Zenica by the 3rd Corps military police was mandatory, is it?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No. If a foreigner is a perpetrator of an offence which comes within the jurisdiction of the military court, then the military police is not duty-bound to react. But for only those criminal offences that I have listed. If a foreigner committed an offence which was not against the army as the damaged party, then this cooperation is not mandatory, but only if the armed forces are the damaged party. Then the same rules apply for civilians and for foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you'd look again at the last sentence of paragraph 50. It just talks about criminal offence. It doesn't talk about, as you stated before, a crime against the army committed by this foreigner or whatever. It just talks about a criminal offence, any criminal offence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No. I have to read the previous sentence: "When criminal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. offences are acted on by the military security service, the competent organ of the military security service is immediately informed thereof and the military police organs undertake measures which brook no delay," so the criminal offences are those directed against the foundations of the social order, as I have already listed. And one would have to look at the Law on Criminal Procedure as well to have full insight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I move on to the Totic abduction. In the aftermath of this abduction occurring on the 15th of April, 1993, were there any joint meetings held between the 3rd Corps, its military police, and the CSB Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Probably yes, but I was not at such a level as to attend such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just -- I'm mentioning two names from the CSB Zenica. Do you know Faik Badic and Enes Saric, who also participated in measures relating to the Totic abduction? Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: It's Faik Spahic and -- not "Badic," and Enes Saric. Yes, I do know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know about their involvement in the investigations relating to Totic's kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any information exchange occurred between the military police of the 3rd Corps and the CSB Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that a broad-based campaign was conducted. Parts of the MP battalion were engaged to escort mixed commissions formed to tour the villages around Zenica, and a second group of members of the military police were engaged for operative work on the ground to collect information about the abduction, and of course there was an exchange of information with members of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So isn't it that when one group had found out something during the search of the terrain or the monitoring of the terrain, that it would report on a kind of conference or meeting on the next day -- it would report simply its results so that by sharing information, the most effective measures were implemented to find Zivko Totic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe so. But I must repeat. I did not attend such meetings, and I don't know how the exchange of information was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has just answered the question. I just wanted to object because the witness said previously that he was not at such a level to be able to attend these meetings. But my learned friend insists on meetings, and I was going to say that there was no grounds for continuing with such line of questioning. But the witness has just repeated the same statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Prosecution, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe your role in the Totic investigation. You were attending the on-site visit in Pobrijezje, I understand, but did you do something else?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I did not go on site. You misunderstood. What I told you here is information that I received from my colleagues who returned from the on-site visit. My role was to collect operative information from citizens, from members of the army, from various entities, information that I was able to get hold of so that as part of this broad-based action we might gain insight into reliable information as to how Mr. Totic was abducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What specific measures did you take and when did you take them? Can you please elaborate a little bit.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: The investigation went on for about four or five days, I think, and the measures I took stemmed from my functional duties, and that is to collect operative knowledge on the ground in the town of Zenica, in the village of Pobrijezje, other villages near Zenica. That is what operative work is all about, working with people who might have some knowledge about the matter, and talking to them I might be able to contribute to the overall investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you took witness statements when talking to certain people in Pobrijezje or in other villages surrounding Zenica, as you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you talked to them - meaning you talked to people - in order to contribute to the overall investigation. These talks which you held, were you taking witness statements or ...?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't talk to witnesses. My work was based on collecting information. As a matter of principle, all inspectors engaging in such activities were able to collect information, but those statements could not be used as evidence in court and they were not relevant in the pre-trial proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned other villages in the surroundings of Zenica. Do you still recall the names of these villages? In which direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: In the direction of the village Pobrijezje, Babino - this is a large area - I said that this went on for three or four days, and I was able to tour those villages, but I also collected information in the town of Zenica itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would show you a map of the area, would you be in a position to point out whereabouts you went?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have also copies for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As a starting point, you have already mentioned the point of the abduction, and you have encircled that on the other map shown by my learned friend. Can you just show where the abduction occurred in Pobrijezje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, if the map could be moved a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle the place Pobrijezje and mark with a "1".

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So where next did you go? Or first of all, what did you do in Pobrijezje, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I came to Podbrezje the next day or the day after. I have some friends there. I tried to find out from them where they had seen anything or heard anything, whether they knew anything about the way in which the abduction took place and about the event itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that Mr. Zivko Totic had been abducted from four unidentified persons -- or rather, four persons had been killed from the escort, that he was kidnapped by unknown people, that Mr. Totic was in a van, a motor vehicle, and that he was driven off in an unknown direction. That was the information I was able to collect in that area. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you know the colour of the van in which Mr. Totic was driven away?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember now. Maybe I knew at the time, but now I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: After that, I was in the town of Zenica itself. I went to the area of this, Babino, Pesivica, Kasapovici, Kula. And I collected information there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you know that on the day, the 15th of April, 1993 -- on the day itself a second on-site visit was conducted in Babino-Rijeka area, that there was a van which was crushed into a bridge fence? Did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't get any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I think there was a misinterpretation. I was told that the van had hit against some sort of boat. But anyway, I hadn't heard anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I was asking for: You said you went to the Babina settlement. There is a document DH340 in evidence, and this document mentions the second on-site visit which was conducted on the 15th of April, 1993 and this second on-site visit was in Babino area exactly where you appear to have been and a red van was found there, a Ford van. Do you recall having been in Babino yourself, having seen that van or having been on the spot?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that a broad action was mobilised and that members of the military police covered a vast area. Babino is a very large area, and I wasn't there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when did you go to Babino, please?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I was there at the beginning of the village. I didn't go further up. It's a mountainous area. Kasapovici Kula. I don't know exactly what day, but that is where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle Babino area for everybody.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: In my understanding, Babino is a vast area covering all these villages. All these villages, Jurjevici, Vranovici, Lijeske. All this is Babino. Kula, Novo Selo. Roughly all of this. It's a very large area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And to the east, can you just mark, because it isn't clear to me as you have marked it -- to the east, where is the eastern border or maybe you cannot even see the eastern border on this map.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: It borders on the municipality of Kakanj, the village of Radinovici [phoen] and many other villages are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So it would be the entire upper right-hand corner of this map basically, as you have halfway encircled it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite. That is the area of Babino, all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection of your recollection, in 1993, which ABiH unit were stationed in this vast area you just described?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that any unit of the army was stationed in that area. The barracks were in the town of Zenica. But territorially they were covered by the anti-sabotage detachments. I don't know which, 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Detachment. So the local population who defended the area from any possibility of saboteurs infiltrating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Anti-sabotage detachment, are you talking about the District Staff in Zenica or the Municipal Staff in Zenica? Just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: These units were subordinated to the Municipal Staff of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Mahir told us you went to Arnauti. Did you yourself go to Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: If he said he was in Arnauti, he probably was. I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So which other -- which are the village did you visit during your time, during your investigations?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I said that the investigation didn't last long, that it was a large area. I went to Kasapovici, Kula. At the beginning of Babino, I was in Podbrezje, and I collected information about potential perpetrators in the town of Zenica. That is what I did over a period of four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please mark Kula. I think it is number 2 or -- I think it's number 2, if you'd encircle it.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Kasapovici, please encircle this and place next to it a "3".

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the reason, to the best of your recollection, that the investigations were focussing on this area?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: The reason was that parallel with these investigations of ours, a mixed commission had been formed which was touring the same area. So we pooled our efforts with the work of the commission, and I, as an inspector in the services department, visited this one area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But my question is: Why focussing on an area south-east of Zenica? Why not on the north-west or other places? To the best of your recollection, why did the main investigative activities focus on this area?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Because that was the assignment I was given. I said that on the first day I went to quite the opposite side, the village of Podbrezje. So that is perhaps north-west. It is quite in the opposite direction. Someone else was assigned to tour some other regions. So what I said was collecting information in the field. This is called "operative work."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle "Arnauti" and place a "4" next to it.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of a village or a hamlet called Gradina?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I think that there's a place called Gradina in Busovaca municipality. I'm not familiar with that village in this area. I only know of a Gradina near Putis in Busovaca municipality, a place called Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There's a Gradina there, but there's also another Gradina 3 to 4 kilometres away from Arnauti, but you obviously haven't heard about this.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I never heard of that Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know in the area where an Uma Maslic [phoen] Elementary School was located?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe that this elementary school is now called Mesa Selimovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would you be in a position to find it on the map?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well, we are talking about a school in Zenica. In Talica Brdo Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No, thank you. This is -- this is another school.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Did you ever hear, either during your military police investigations or otherwise, that certain individuals were involved in kidnapping Mr. Totic? Did you hear any names?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't hear names. I believe that the investigation was interrupted because an international organisation the name of which I can't remember at the moment asked for the investigation to be called off because they feared for the security of the kidnapped person, and that's why the investigation was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear mention of the name Ramo Durmis in relation to the investigation or in relation to the abduction of Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I can't remember ever hearing -- that I ever heard anybody Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mentioning that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the name Sabahudin Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't want to interrupt my learned friend; however, the past several questions have had nothing to do with my questions or the answers that the witness has provided so far. If my learned friend thinks that he has reason for these questions to be put, then he has to lay a legal foundation for asking questions about certain persons and names. So far he has mentioned two names without laying any legal foundation for such questions. And I think that this shouldn't be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you've heard the objection by the Defence. Could you tell us what are you trying to achieve. What have you established with regard to Ramo Durmis and how could this witness be involved with that person? The Defence says that they haven't mentioned this name in their examination-in-chief, and if you want to mention this name, if you want to ask the witness about this person, what is your foundation? What are the legal grounds for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, the -- my learned friend has put several questions in relation to the Totic abduction, and I think this is the first time that now through the map and all the places which were indeed visited by this witness, that we see where the scope of the main investigative activity was. And the very fact that the Prosecution is asking for some knowledge about whether certain names came up in investigation is just a way of exploring what the witness may know. He is free to say, "I have never heard these names during my investigation." That's indeed the aim of the Prosecution, just to find out whether certain names and knowledge about certain names existed at a certain period in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you may proceed in asking whether in his investigation he heard certain names being mentioned, and we shall see whether he says yes or no. If he says yes, then you can ask him whether he knows Adilovic or Durmis. You may repeat your question. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, since I have mentioned the name Ramo Durmis already, does the name Ramo Durmis -- not necessarily in relation to Totic -- have you ever heard the name Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of Ramo Durmis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what you have heard about him.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I first learned of him towards the end of 1992 during the fighting for deblocking the city of Sarajevo. At that time, he clashed with certain commanders in the territory of Visoko, and I believe that my colleagues investigated the matter. And that's when I first heard of Ramo Durmis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you know what type of investigation was launched by your colleagues? Did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I was not directly involved, and it was a long time ago, in 1992. I really can't tell you with any degree of certainty about the investigation. I only know what I've just told you, that there was an investigation of some sort because Ramo Durmis had clashed with the commanders with regard to the number of casualties in the Visoko theatre of war or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Other than -- other than that, do you know anything else about Ramo Durmis, especially in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: After that, his name was often mentioned in our services because he was a member of one unit and then -- and then he was not a member of any unit. He was often searched by our services. Nobody knew where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you elaborate a little bit? In which unit was he a member, first?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't even know whether he was an army member or not. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So only your colleagues had any investigations against Ramo Durmis? You said he was a kind of known person or -- if I can just ask: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness never said that many persons -- many people knew of him. He just said that his name was often mentioned in various searches and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is exactly what the witness has told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It says here in the transcript, and I'm quoting from page 66, line 2: "He" - meaning Ramo Durmis- "was often searched by our services." Often.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may just ask: He was often searched in relation to investigations, in relation to particular incidents? Do you know anything?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything specific, and I don't wish to speculate. I've heard of the name. The name does ring a bell. I know that he was mentioned later on. I don't know what the context was. I don't know whether he was a member of the army or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has already answered that question. This has been answered -- asked and answered at least two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, it is twenty to 6.00. I have to make a break. We have already worked for an hour and a half. We shall now adjourn and we will resume around five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: After the release of Mr. Totic, investigative activities were again possible. Did you engage again in investigative activities, or your unit?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I was never given any specific orders with regard to that case. I personally did not receive any tasks, and I don't know if anybody else did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So from the 18th of May, when Mr. Totic -- 1993, when Mr. Totic was released, you weren't engaging in any investigative activities to find the perpetrators of the abduction of Mr. Totic.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: It was the 18th of April, not the 18th of May. I didn't say that there were no investigations. I said that I was not involved in any investigations. I mentioned the settlement of Raspotocje, and I was engaged in the disarmament of this battalion that I mentioned earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was referring to the period after his release, which is, I believe, 18th of May, 1993 onwards. And I was just asking whether you -- and I understood you didn't perform any further investigative activities, isn't it? In relation to the Totic kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I did not carry out any investigation. I don't know whether anybody else from the military police did. They may have done that, but I don't know whether they did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever file a criminal report relating to Totic kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I said that an investigative judge was on the scene. A prosecutor was also there. And they were in charge of the investigation. We worked on their orders, on the order of the investigative judge, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could, with the assistance of the usher, have the map my learned friend has used at the end of her examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just asking you to point, if you know, to the headquarter of Zivko Totic, where he was abducted on the 15th of April and I think he was -- you have marked the point where he was abducted. If you could just show where his headquarter is, please. Point to it.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I said that it was approximately here. I can't be more precise than that. I know that the command of this brigade of the Jure Francetic Brigade was in the administrative building of the Vatrostalna company in Podbrezje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just make a cross where this Vatrostalna company or Totic's headquarters is.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you for the benefit of the Trial Chamber say how many kilometres it is from this Vatrostalna enterprise premise to the 3rd headquarters, how many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: The distance as the crow flies is not large. However, from the command of the Jure Francetic to the other command, you have to go around the ironworks. You could not cut through the ironworks directly. So it could be some 10 kilometres or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saric, you said who you reported to with regard to the interviews that you had with the captured persons from Lasva. You said that you drafted an official record and that it went to the security organ of the 3rd Corps. Do you know who the chief of the security sector was in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: In January 1993, it could have been Tadija Brekalo or Avdic Nasif. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since my learned friend mentioned Ramiz Dugalic, do you know when he was appointed the chief of the security sector of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was somewhat later, in March, or even the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My learned friend showed you P327, which is the rules of the work of the military police. Could we look at the document once again, the Rules of Service for the military police. Could we look at paragraph 328 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is P328, not P327.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. It is 328.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Article 50 under 7, "Crime prevention service." In response to my learned friend's question, you said that the joint work of the military police and the Security Services Centre was always carried out when the crimes falling under the jurisdiction of the district military court which are prosecuted ex officio are perpetrated by other persons, civilians or foreigners who were treated as civilians. Is that what you said in response to my learned friend's question?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the first sentence of Article 50.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: "If a person is suspected of committing an offence within the jurisdiction of the military court which is prosecuted ex officio, authorised members of the military police have the duty to undertake the necessary measures to locate the perpetrator of the criminal offence, to see that the offender or accomplice should not go into hiding or escape and to uncover or protect the traces of a criminal act and any objects which can be used as evidence and to assemble all information liable to be useful for a successful trial."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Saric: The first sentence that you have just read out, doesn't it clearly show that you only acted when a crime was committed that fell within the jurisdiction of the military court?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you read only the last sentence, you may have a different impression. However, if you read the entire context, you will be clear on the contents of this article.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also told us that after the kidnapping of Mr. Zivko Totic you had a task to collect certain operative information. Mr. Saric, this collection of operative information on the ground, did it have to assume a certain form, or was it still an informal part of the pre-criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. This was an informal part of the pre-criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your capacity as the inspector of the criminal -- of the military police, when you found yourself in a position to take a statement, were you ever authorised to interview a person as a witness?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the nature of the statement given to the police, either to the civilian police or the military police?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: It could not be used as evidence in criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could it ever be used in criminal proceedings or -- or shown to the person who had given that statement?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I've already answered that. It did not have any value in criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you took statements from certain persons who might eventually become suspects during the formal part of your pre-criminal procedure, did these persons have to tell the truth? Did you warn them about their obligation to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to formulate an objection. The last question was leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see how it was leading, but I can rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, rephrase it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Saric, how do you take statements for suspects? In our law -- or under our law, are these persons obliged to tell the truth in the informal or the formal part of the procedure?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, during our part of the procedure, they were not obliged to do that. They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's again leading. The question is leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you very much. I don't know how to put that question. I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Try to be up to the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Saric, given the fact that witnesses are interviewed like you are being interviewed today after having taken a statement, are you aware of the fact that our Penal Code contained a similar provision on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. testimony of a suspect? Was a suspect ever obliged or warned to tell the truth after taking an oath?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: In our procedure, this was not an obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No additional questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, it seems that there is an error in the transcript. Could you please tell us, what is your date of birth exactly? Because in the transcript, it says "1996". I believe that this is a mistake. Could you please tell us your year of birth.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: My son was born in 1996. I was born in 1966.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Thank you for this clarification. In answering one question, you said that the military police of the 3rd Corps was of the strength of 200 to 250 men. Is that a good figure, or was that a mistake on your part?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, the figure was anything between 200 and 250 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how were they distributed, these military policemen of the 3rd Corps? What was their distribution? How were they spread?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you, they were distributed across four companies. There was also an anti-terrorist group, and the companies numbered a similar number of men. And as our tasks and missions increased, there was a need to increase the numbers of men. We became a battalion, and when it became a battalion towards the end of the year, according to my free estimates, it had about 400 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You yourself, you were a member of what part? Of the Department for Services?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I was an inspector in the Department for Services of the Battalion of the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For how long were you an inspector and how many inspectors were there?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Between eight and ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said at the beginning that -- of your testimony that before you became an inspector you worked at an airport, and I believe that you were a member of the JNA. In order to become a military policeman, you need a certain education. Were you educated as a military policeman? What did you do at that airport that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: At the Zemunik airport, I was a technician for airplanes and engines. I was a member of the Air Force. And when I joined -- and when I joined the Territorial Defence Staff, there was a need for officers in the military police unit and I and some other officers who had occupied the various positions before that in the former JNA joined the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But how do you explain the fact that a technician for engines could become a military policeman? Do you have an explanation for that? How is -- how was that possible?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: My explanation is the state of war. The few people who were military policemen were not enough for the military battalion. There was a much greater need. The battalion was replenished successively and the organ of the security service drafted plans. There were seminars. There were training courses. And that's how military policemen were trained, and they could join the Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As an inspector, did you wear a uniform of a military policeman? How were you dressed? Could you describe your apparel. Did you have insignia? Did you have a badge? How were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I wore a uniform, and if the need arose, I would wear civilian clothes. With permission of my superior commander, I was allowed to wear civilian clothes when the need arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. So you could work in civilian clothes, in plain clothes.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, when it proved to be necessary and upon approval of the superior command and especially the Centre of Military Security Services via the battalion command. That is how the approval was handed down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At your level of inspector, were you aware of the existence of an individual who got hold of the uniform of a military policeman and pretended to be a military policeman but he wasn't one? Are you aware of such a phenomenon, of such cases?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I think that I said in my testimony that there were a large number of people wearing different uniforms, and there were cases when certain members would falsely pretend to be military policemen. There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as far as you know, were there any -- was there any persecution or punishment of people who usurped their positions and pretended to be something they were not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but I think there were cases of false presentations. And if they were found out, they were reported. Because we had precise instructions from the corps command via the battalion command that all persons should be treated in accordance with the law, that there should be no exception from criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll come to the abduction of Totic. You told us that you took part, at least at the very beginning, in the investigation. When your service learned that Totic was abducted, what was Totic's status for your service? Was Totic treated as a military man or as a civilian by you?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Zivko Totic was commander of a brigade. He was a soldier. The Jure Francetic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. So Totic was a military man. And being a member of the military, who is the competent prosecutor? The military or the civilian prosecutor? In your opinion.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I think the military prosecutor would be competent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the military prosecutor. And if Totic was kidnapped by civilians, who is competent? Is it still the military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: If they were civilians, then it would be the civilian prosecutor. If the perpetrators were civilians ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But at the beginning, nobody knew who abducted him. It could have been military people or civilians, when you conducted your investigations.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is why the duty judge from the district military court went on site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. When Mr. Totic was freed and exchanged, where were you?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: In May 1993 - I think the Prosecutor said that this was in May 1993 - I was in Zenica. I was engaged in other military policework within my competence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were not present at the "release" of Mr. Totic.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No. No, I was not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there talk by people around you about the way that he was released? Did you know who kidnapped him?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any precise information about that. I can't remember what exactly was going on. I just know that he was exchanged. Now, who abducted him or kidnapped him, I really didn't know at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the event that those who released him were civilians, or liberated him, who would be competent to continue the investigation?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: If it was civilians, then it would be the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During your investigation, did you learn that at the time of the kidnapping there was a civilian who was killed? Did you know that or not? Apparently it was by accident that this civilian was nearby where the shooting took place. Did you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: As I was saying, I didn't go on site. I don't have precise information. I know that the duty judge was there and he must have established that on site, if that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, in fact, you can't help us at all regarding the follow-up to this investigation about the kidnapping and the killing of a civilian, so you have no information to provide?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I do not have any precise information. I was not in charge of this. For four days I did collect information from the area. I didn't go on site, and I can't give you any precise information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A final question for you: A moment ago the Prosecution showed you a plan and asked you to mark the places that you visited. The village of Arnauti was mentioned. I didn't quite grasp whether you went to Arnauti and why this name appeared. Could you tell us. You yourself, did you go to Arnauti or not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I did not go to Arnauti, but all the villages were mentioned. I know a mixed commission was working simultaneously visiting military facilities around Zenica, including the village of Arnauti, but I didn't go there. I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the joint commission, it didn't ask for aid from you, from the Military Police Battalion of the 3rd Corps? Did you assist them or not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, some members, as I have said, escorted the members of that commission. They accompanied them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you yourself, did you accompany them? Did you contribute to this joint commission?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I did not. I had other assignments. My assignment was to collect operative information from a particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the answers you have given to the points I wished to clear up. I shall give the floor once again to the Prosecution, if they wish to take the floor after me, and then I shall give the floor to the Defence. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago - this is page 78, line 14 - that there was a mixed commission who was visiting military facilities surrounding Zenica, including Arnauti. Did the commission only visit military facilities or other facilities too?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I believe that in the village of Arnauti there are no special military facilities. As far as I know - I didn't go there, but I know from stories - you yourself said that they went there, and all the facilities were visited in which they thought that a kidnapped person may possibly be held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All facilities were visited in which the person was -- or "may possibly be held," you just said. Are we talking about elementary schools, about public buildings, or are we talking also about private buildings, or religious buildings?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR SARIC
utterances.text: I wasn't a member of that commission, nor did I accompany that commission, so I don't know exactly what they toured or what information they collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have a question, but I wish to note that on page 79, line 15 the witness said "colleague Mahir was there, as you yourself said." And the name was not included in the transcript. The name is "Mahir." It's a witness we heard here a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that specification. The other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, captain, your hearing is completed. Thank you for coming to The Hague at the request of the Defence to testify. You have answered all the questions -- Mr. Neuner, for the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's only about the map. Before the witness is released, if I may ask the witness to sign the map and add today's date. It's the 14th of March. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I thought you had already done that. Put your name on the map and the date, the 14th of March, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll give the map to the registrar now. As I was saying, thank you for testifying. On behalf of the Chamber, best wishes for your return journey. And I'm going to ask the usher to be kind enough to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the documents, I shall give the floor to the Defence. I don't think they have any documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We would like the map marked by the witness to be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It is admitted as Defence Exhibit DH2080. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We would like also to tender one map into evidence. It's an excerpt I believe from P1. It's dealing with Zenica and its surroundings, including Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no objection, but for the record we would like to say that the witness marked the village of Arnauti but he made it clear that he did not visit that village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely why I asked him the question, and he confirmed that he didn't go there. Mr. Registrar, can you give us a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This map is admitted as Prosecutor's Exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit P958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the schedule for the rest of the week, the Defence, please. Do you wish us to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Registrar, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
